change: mruby port patch 0010 backports upstream e5c82761f (envadjust rebases off the new stack). It unblocks MRBD_HEAP=sublet and sublet-gc, which until now failed their own control, and the 165-case corpus then runs in all three arms.

defect.what: stack_extend_alloc() hands the old VM stack to mrb_realloc() and then calls envadjust(), which moved each frame with ci->stack += delta -- pointer arithmetic on a pointer realloc has already freed
defect.why_it_matters_here: on an allocator whose free revokes, the result is derived from a revoked capability, carries no tag, and the next write through it faults (cause 24)
defect.upstream: e5c82761f 'vm.c: fix envadjust rebasing stack pointers off a freed pointer' (2026-07-24), found when another memory-safe C implementation trapped on the same write. Its diff does not apply at this pin because it rewrites the byte-level form from d95ebe4a2, which landed after the pin; the expression it settles on is used verbatim.
defect.pins: only 4.0.0-rc2 needs it: the port's head pin ad98f216e carries both d95ebe4a2 and e5c82761f (checked with merge-base --is-ancestor)

before.symptom: sublet and sublet-gc faulted at ~40 frames of Ruby recursion, shallow enough that the port's own scripts/smoke.rb stopped at M8
before.bracket: one recursion depth per run, same script in all three arms: level0 completed at 20/40/60/100/200/500; sublet and sublet-gc completed at 20 and faulted at 40 and above

after.controls: all three arms complete scripts/smoke.rb (SMOKE_DONE) and deep(500)
after.node_pool_note: CAPSTONE_REV_NODES=16777216 was needed on this kit. dev's sublet_heap.c (PR #158) says the 65,536-identity pool bounds live identities rather than allocations per boot, because capstone-qemu recycles retired identities since 22aec7ee0f. That commit is NOT in the capstone-qemu this kit's emulator was built from (it is not an ancestor of the checked-out HEAD 408fd83945), and the A/B here shows the older behaviour: same images, the control dies at M5 on the 65,536 default and completes at 16,777,216. So this figure is a property of the kit's emulator, not a contradiction of that comment

corpus_165.criterion: a catch is a case the control runs to completion and a revoking arm faults on; level0 revokes nothing, so its own faults are the defect reaching a bounds or tag check and are not catches

caught.subject: mruby-sprintf: protect format string from mutation during call
caught.note: the control completes silently and both revoking arms fault: the cleanest catch in the set

caught.subject: hash.c: keep the pair a scan carries into a set alive across it
caught.note: revoke-on-free does not reach it; per-slot revocation does

caught.subject: mruby-task: mark the main task's values during GC
caught.note: ASan is blind to it at the default page size and revoke-on-free misses it; only per-GC-slot revocation catches it. Reachable at all only because the port now builds mruby-task

caught.subject: mruby-hash-ext: keep what a walk carries out of a hash alive
caught.note: same shape: the slot layer sees it, the heap layer does not

instrument_note: the first run of the revoking arms was void and is not reported: run-arm.sh set CAPSTONE_REV_NODES only for arms named exactly sublet or sublet-gc, and these are named fx-sublet, so both ran on the 65536 default and their control stopped at M5. The arm-name match is now a glob, and the control is read before any case verdict.
